analysis:
Both units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 209-746). The only visible change is documentation: the head replaces the v0.10.1 candidate header with v0.10.2 and adds about 230 lines of release notes at head lines 11-246. Those added lines are not in the supplied units; only a truncated patch excerpt shows them. I treated the base text as context and found no code, configuration, permission or workflow change in the supplied evidence.

The visible patch lines describe rollout items touching T-041 (prefix-cache SSD tier) and T-053-adjacent routing:
- 4-bit 'balanced' SSD checkpoints for Nemotron Super and GLM, written under new cache namespaces, so old files miss once and age out via the TTL sweep.
- Coordinator cache-routing allowlist gating by (model_id, aggregate, prompt_contract_id).
- Logprobs exposed only once the catalog row lists them and the fleet has converged.

The excerpt states 4-bit checkpoint outputs are not bit-identical to uncached ones, with logprob deltas. That is a documented behavioral caveat, not a control regression. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the remaining v0.10.2 notes were not reviewed. T-041's detection hint says changes to TTL, disk budget, lookup-key derivation, DBK3 metadata or salt scoping need review. The excerpt shows no such change, but the underlying provider-swift source changes (cache namespace, quantized checkpoints, logprobs ingress) are not in this batch. Integration should confirm that the 4-bit checkpoint format keeps the HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping, TTL of at most 30 minutes, and AAD-bound metadata unchanged, and that logprobs requests cannot bypass cache-scope partitioning.

Other base-text items already in the base changelog (Nemotron media limits, video decode bounds, staging release lane relaxing the installer signature check for -dev./-staging. versions) are pre-existing and not attributable to this PR.

No findings from these units. Deeper review is warranted for the non-visible code that the changelog describes.
